newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian central bank uncovers $14 million fraud.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian central bank uncovers $14 million fraud.

text.p: Nigeria's central bank has uncovered a 1.115 billion naira ($14 million) fraud involving the national environment agency and a commercial bank, the national news agency said on Sunday.

The News Agency of Nigeria said the central bank had accused the Federal Environmental Protection Agency (FEPA) and Pinacle Commercial Bank of "abuse of the clearing system (through) the issue of eight dud cheques".
Nigeria, Africa's most populous nation, has won an unenviable reputation for fraudulent deals.

In an effort to sanitise the banking industry the military government has detained dozens of bank directors who played a part in the collapse of banks in the early 1990s, many of them allegedly through fraud.
"A comprehensive report on the role played by FEPA in the abuse of the clearing house system shall be presented to the presidency," the agency said.
